To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sequences flanking a core DNA binding domain contribute to the affinity of the protein for its target DNA, stabilize the protein against denaturing, and contribute to function.
the minimal DNA-binding domain of E2 is not sufficient for DNA binding and that sequences flanking this core domain are an integral part of this domain.
the flanking regions of the DNA-binding core domain of BPV E2 contribute to the DNA-binding function and stability of the protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that sequences flanking a protein domain play in protein function.
the structure and function of E2 proteins of the papilloma virus family and their interactions with cellular factors.
the role of the amino- and carboxy-terminal flanking sequences on the DNA-binding function of BPV-2 and BPV-1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the E2 protein contains two domains: a core DNA-binding domain that is sufficient for dimerization and DNA-binding function and a flanking region which contributes to the affinity of E1 and E2 for their target DNA.

the E2 protein of BPV- 1 is a DNA-binding protein that has the ability to bind to its target sequence in a cooperative manner and that the flanking sequences of the core domain are an integral part of this function.
the DNA-binding domain is not the core DNA-binding and dmerization domain but rather the entire region between amino acid residues 5 and 50.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the E2 core domain, which contains the DNA-binding site, is composed of two parts, the core domain proper (amino acids 2 to 80) and the flanking sequences (amino acids +1 to +16).
sequences adjacent to the core DNA-binding and dmerization domains of BPV- 1 E2 are required for high-affinity DNA binding and for protein stability.

the core DNA-binding and dmerization domain of E2 is composed of three parts, each of which is required for function: a core DNA-binding and oligomerization domain, a flanking region that enhances DNA binding, and a C-terminal domain that contains the nuclear localization and activation signals of E2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flanking sequences of the core DNA-binding region of BPV- 1 E2 are an integral part of this region and contribute to DNA binding and dimerization of the protein.
the flanking sequences are not just a spacer but are a part of the DNA binding domain of BPV E2.

the DNA-binding domains of BPV-2 and BPV-1 differ significantly in their ability to bind to DNA in the absence of the flanking region, suggesting that the flanking regions may be more important for BPV-1 than for BPV-2 E2 function.
